title: Asset Manifest
description:
Every asset the game needs, its source, its cost, and its status.

This is an ARTIFACT, not a stage. There is deliberately no asset-production state: serializing art behind a gate would put code behind art and wreck a 7-14 day schedule. Asset work happens inside prototype and production, tracked here as line-item status, and `complete` becomes a guard on production exit.

It is authored during design because asset cost is an input to the scope decision — and an input cannot be produced downstream of the decision it feeds.

dimension.description: Which renderer the asset is for. Audio and fonts take the game's dimension.

source.description: Drives both cost and licensing risk. Library and procedural are the cheap paths and should be preferred at this scale.

license.description: An SPDX identifier, or a LicenseRef- id from core/reference/asset-policy.yaml. Required before a purchased, library or commissioned asset can be integrated. An unlicensed asset in a published build is a real liability, not a paperwork detail.

license_status.description: The license classified against core/reference/asset-policy.yaml. generated: made by the Factory, owing nobody. verified: a permitted license with a recorded origin. restricted: a license the policy forbids in a published build. unknown: missing or unrecognised, and treated exactly like missing.

usage_constraints.description: What using the asset obliges - attribution, share-alike, keep-receipt - from the license's policy entry plus anything the source adds.

origin.description: Where the asset came from. Required in substance for every asset the Factory did not generate: without it a license is an assertion nobody can check.

generator.description: For a generated asset, the backend that made it.

library_id.description: For a library asset, its entry in the library index.

attribution.description: The credits line, verbatim, when the license requires one.

evidence.description: Where the proof of license lives: a receipt, a contract, an archived page.

placeholder.description: A stand-in generated so code is not blocked on art. Never production-ready.

production_ready.description: Valid, license-cleared and not a placeholder. Always false when license_status is unknown or restricted: unknown licensing must not silently become a production asset.

files.description: The delivered files, relative to the game repository root. A spritesheet has an image and its atlas.

reference.description: For an asset delivered as a named fallback rather than a file, such as a system font stack.

applied.description: Lossless steps already done to the delivered files.

deferred.description: Pipeline steps still owed, from the policy's optimize list.

issues.description: Issue codes on this item. The details are in the manifest's issues list.

pipeline.description: How source assets become runtime assets. 3D adds compression steps that materially change load time on mobile web.

complete.description: True when every non-cut item is integrated. Part of the content_complete guard on production exit — which is why CONTENT COMPLETE is not a lifecycle state.

policy.description: The asset policy the items were classified against, pinned by hash so a re-classification is visible.

issues.description: Everything wrong with the manifest, one entry per problem. An error keeps its item from being production-ready.

generation.description: Which placeholder backends were tried. An optional backend that is unavailable is recorded, never fatal.
